title: check
description: Coverage of Triauth.check: argument validation (101/102), identifier validation (210-216), DNS resolution failure (110), and the success/failure paths through Identity.resolve() + IdentityKeys.findByTag().

null options arg returns 102 — hasOnlyKnownProperties null-guard at src/helpers.js:236 fires before any other check
array options arg returns 102 — hasOnlyKnownProperties Array.isArray-guard at src/helpers.js:236 fires before any other check
empty options object returns 101 (typeof identifier !== 'string' guard at src/api/authentication.js:298)
missing deviceTag returns 101 (typeof deviceTag !== 'string' guard)
missing identifier returns 101

non-string deviceTag (number) returns 101
unrecognized option returns 102 — hasOnlyKnownProperties guard at src/api/authentication.js:289 fires before the typeof check
identifier with whitespace returns 210 — passes the typeof/empty/byteSize guards but hits the /[\s\0]/ check at src/validator.js:75
empty-string identifier returns 211

tests.name: identifier missing @-sign returns 214
identifier with consecutive dots in username returns 215

DNS SERVFAIL on identifier domain — resolveConfig throws TriauthError(110) in AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve(), propagates through identity.resolve() and is caught by check()'s try/catch

tests.name: domain not configured for triauth returns valid:false — AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve() returns false (no triauth TXT record), identity.resolved becomes false, check returns {valid:false, reason:'unresolved'}

resolution order: endpoint is resolved before the identity domain — the domain publishes no triauth record while its would-be identity domain would SERVFAIL; check returns {valid:false, reason:'unresolved'} (not error 110), so the identity-domain query is never issued (src/identity.js:88-94)

domain with multiple triauth TXT records returns valid:false — AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve() takes the 'refuse to choose' branch at src/authentication_endpoint.js:90, resets this.url to null, identity.resolved becomes false. Distinct from the no-record path; this exercises the multi-record reset.
endpoint record with an unknown mode (mode=banana) returns valid:false reason:unresolved - no identity domain can be derived
endpoint record without a mode option runs the domain in private mode by default - a bare deviceTag carries no lookup code, so the identity cannot resolve (valid:false reason:unresolved)

identity records contain a malformed key that taints the device group (desktop[2/1]: keyIdx 2 > keyCount 1) returns valid:false — IdentityKeys.add marks keyGroup.tainted at src/identity_keys.js:130, no tag is ever computed, findByTag's `keyGroup.valid &&` short-circuit skips the group. Distinct from the no-keys path because keyGroups[deviceName] DOES exist.

key-count disagreement across a device's records (dev[1/2] + dev[2/3]) taints the group — keyGroup.keyCount is fixed by the first record and a mismatched declaration trips the consistency check at src/identity_keys.js:139, findByTag skips the tainted group, valid:false reason:'revoked'

duplicate key index within a device (two dev[1/2] records) taints the group — keyGroup.keys[keyIdx-1] is already occupied when the second record arrives (src/identity_keys.js:140), valid:false reason:'revoked'
key data longer than 1024 characters taints the group — the length cap at src/identity_keys.js:141 fires even though every character is base64url, valid:false reason:'revoked'
key data with characters outside the base64url alphabet (abc!def) taints the group — isBase64UrlString fails at src/identity_keys.js:142, valid:false reason:'revoked'
device declaring key-count 6 (dev[1/6]) taints the group — keyCount exceeds LIMITS.maxKeysPerDevice=5 at src/identity_keys.js:137, valid:false reason:'revoked'

SECURITY: split key group with only its final fragment published (dev[2/2] alone, no dev[1/2]) never becomes valid — the validity gate counts populated slots (Object.keys in src/identity_keys.js), not keys.length, which a lone write to the last index already inflates to keyCount; the supplied deviceTag is the exact digest a single populated entry would hash to, so a length-gated implementation answers valid:true here — findByTag must find no valid group, valid:false reason:'revoked'
configured domain but unknown identifier returns valid:false — authentication endpoint resolves, identity domain returns empty record set, identity.resolved becomes false
identity records exist but contain no key entries returns valid:false — identity.resolved is true (records present), but findByTag returns null because no keys were added
wrong deviceTag for an otherwise resolvable identity returns valid:false — findByTag returns null because no keyGroup matches the tag
empty deviceTag returns valid:false — passes the typeof guard (empty string is still a string) but findByTag returns null
per-test dnsEntries patch can NXDOMAIN the identifier domain (null overrides suite-level entry), surfacing as valid:false
valid device tag for known identifier returns valid:true with secure:true and expires = now + ttl*1000

key record with dnssec:false yields secure:false in the result; ttl:60 yields expires = now + 60_000 — a non-DNSSEC record makes the resolution-level secure false (DNSSEC validates the answer, not individual records)

security: deviceTag is scoped per-identity — john's tag does not validate under a different identifier whose identity records publish a different key. Pins that findByTag is bounded by the resolved Identity instance; a refactor that turns findByTag into a global lookup would regress this.

security: shared device → equal tag — two identifiers that legitimately publish the same deviceName + key value + options produce identical tags, so john's tag validates against the 'shared' identity. Pins this as expected behavior (key sharing across identities is allowed by the protocol) so a future 'tags must be unique per identity' change is a deliberate decision, not an accident.

security: secure is resolution-level — laptop has 2 keys, one with dnssec:true and one with dnssec:false; a single non-validated record of the identity answer makes the whole resolution insecure. Pins that one insecure record downgrades secure. (Contrast with the dimly test, which has a single-key device.)

expires is MIN-across-keys within a device — laptop has 2 keys with ttl:60 and ttl:300 (both dnssec:true); keyGroup.expires takes the earlier expiry at src/identity_keys.js:175, so check returns currentTime + 60_000. (Companion to the AND-across-keys secure case.)

security: tainted device does not shadow a valid device on the same identity — identity publishes a well-formed desktop AND a malformed bogus[2/1]; bogus gets tainted at src/identity_keys.js:130 but findByTag iterates Object.values(keyGroups) and the desktop's valid keyGroup is still returned. Pins that poisoned records can't break verification of the rest.

security: ttl:0 yields expires === currentTime (numeric, not undefined) — pins the 'must be a Number' branch at src/identity.js:94 so a future refactor that collapses ttl:0 to undefined (F4) is caught. The keyGroup is still valid; the caller's responsibility is to act on the expires timestamp.

security: identifier at the exact identifierBytesize boundary (120 bytes) passes validation — inverse of the 212 case; the byteSize check is strict-greater (> 120). No DNS records exist for this domain → valid:false (not an error).
security: a `+` in the username (john+@) fails validation with 215 - `+` is not a username character
SECURITY: endpoint triauth record with dnssec:false caps secure to false even though the key records are DNSSEC-validated
SECURITY: uv=required on a non-webauthn (es256) key is unenforceable and taints the keyGroup -> valid:false - fail closed
key record with type=ed25519 forms a valid keyGroup; a matching deviceTag returns valid:true (requires the ed25519 verifier to be registered)
mixed-type device (es256 + ed25519 keys) forms one valid keyGroup whose deviceTag covers both keys with their type options
SECURITY: uv=required on an ed25519 (non-webauthn) key is unenforceable and taints the keyGroup -> valid:false - fail closed
requireSecure: check stage 3 - DNSSEC-secure result still succeeds when requireSecure:true
SECURITY requireSecure: check stage 3 - non-DNSSEC (secure:false) result is rejected with 404

error.message: Your domain does not support DNSSEC, which is required to continue.

tests.name: requireSecure: check stage - revoked keys still return {valid:false} (valid:false path not gated)
key index 0 (dev[0/1]) is out of the 1..keyCount range and taints the group - valid:false reason:'revoked'
leading-zero key index (dev[01/1]) taints the group - the wire grammar admits no leading zeros, and a lenient parseInt port that reads 01 as 1 must be caught here; valid:false reason:'revoked'
unknown critical option key (color=blue) on a Key Record taints the group - only x-* option keys are experimental; valid:false reason:'revoked'
unregistered key type (type=banana) taints the group - the registry's unknown-value rule for key types; valid:false reason:'revoked'
unknown use element (use=auth,banana) taints the group - the registry's unknown-value rule for key uses; valid:false reason:'revoked'
len option present on a public-mode endpoint (mode=public len=banana) is inert - len is not an option key, so it is retained without effect and check succeeds
delegated deviceTag with a matching include grant returns valid:true - check is a liveness re-find: the grant is use=sign yet check (which carries no flow) accepts it
SECURITY: composite check with the pinned include record served without DNSSEC -> valid:true with secure:false - the subject-side resolution degrades the two-resolution AND
SECURITY: composite check with the actor's key record served without DNSSEC -> valid:true with secure:false - the actor-side resolution degrades the two-resolution AND
GROUPS: check valid:true carries the identity's current groups, fully qualified, deduplicated, and sorted
GROUPS: membership freshness - the same deviceTag against changed groups records returns the new list (periodic check replaces session-cached groups)
GROUPS: composite-tag delegated check carries the SUBJECT's groups, not the actor's
delegated deviceTag whose include grant is no longer published returns valid:false reason:revoked
delegated deviceTag pinned to a DIFFERENT grant tag returns valid:false reason:revoked (the tag covers the ref and its critical options)
delegated deviceTag whose pinned grant is scoped to another service (use=sign scope=other.example) returns valid:true - check carries no flow and no callback URL, so liveness is scope-blind

SECURITY: delegated deviceTag pinned to the scope=any grant tag returns valid:false reason:revoked when the published grant carries a host list - scope folds into the grant tag, so editing it ends sessions established under the grant

SECURITY: delegated deviceTag pinned to the scope=any grant tag returns valid:false reason:revoked when the published grant lacks scope - the record is ignored as a whole, so no grant matches the pinned tag
delegated deviceTag whose actor identity cannot be resolved returns valid:false reason:unresolved (distinct from revocation - the grant is still published)
malformed composite deviceTag (two segments) returns valid:false reason:revoked
malformed composite deviceTag (non-lowercase actor identifier) returns valid:false reason:revoked
include grant published as the 50th include record (at LIMITS.maxIncludes) is honored - the cap admits exactly maxIncludes grants
include grant published as the 51st include record (past LIMITS.maxIncludes=50) is skipped - the first 50 grants stay live, only the excess is ignored - returns valid:false reason:revoked
PRIVATE: direct deviceTag with a ~lookupCode suffix under a private-mode domain returns valid:true - the code re-derives the identity domain and the commitment binds the records
PRIVATE: a triauth record without a mode option runs the domain in private mode by default - a ~lookupCode deviceTag returns valid:true

PRIVATE: a published len option on a private-mode endpoint (mode=private len=3) is inert - len is not an option key, the label stays 10 characters, so the identity resolves at the same identity domain and check succeeds
PRIVATE: fully suffixed delegated walk (grantTag~code:actor:devTag~actorCode, both zones in private mode) returns valid:true - each tag component carries the lookup code of the zone it resolves in
PRIVATE: subject-only suffixed delegated walk (private-mode subject, public-mode actor) returns valid:true - only the grant component carries a lookup code

PRIVATE: actor-only suffixed delegated walk (public-mode subject, private-mode actor) returns valid:true - only the device component carries a lookup code, and the actor's own commitment binds its records
PRIVATE: a suffix-less direct deviceTag under a private-mode domain returns valid:false reason:unresolved - the identity domain cannot derive without the lookup code

PRIVATE: a ~lookupCode suffix on a deviceTag under a public-mode domain returns valid:true - the walk strips the suffix before comparing bare digests, so a handle minted while the domain ran mode=private keeps resolving after the domain switches away from it
PRIVATE: a 15-character lookup-code suffix (one under the exact 16) returns valid:false reason:unresolved
PRIVATE: a lowercase lookup-code suffix returns valid:false reason:unresolved - the [A-Z0-9]{16} grammar is strict, with no case folding
PRIVATE: a well-formed but wrong lookup-code suffix derives an unpublished identity domain and returns valid:false reason:unresolved
PRIVATE SECURITY: a ~lookupCode on the ACTOR component returns valid:false reason:revoked - codes attach to tag components only, and an actor identifier carrying '~' fails the identifier grammar

PRIVATE: a ~lookupCode on the grant component under a PUBLIC-mode subject returns valid:false reason:revoked - the suffix is stripped before the grant tag is matched, and this public-mode subject publishes no such grant
PRIVATE SECURITY: a mismatched commit record returns valid:false reason:unresolved - a failed binding is treated as publishing no records
PRIVATE: a revoked actor device under the fully suffixed walk returns valid:false reason:revoked - the actor's zone no longer publishes the worker device
PRIVATE: a commit record served without DNSSEC returns valid:true with secure:false - the binding verifies while the resolution-level status degrades
